accuracy.evidence: Every number was recomputed: means 42 + 44 + 43 = 129, ÷ 3 = 43 cm; 12 + 14 + 13 = 39, ÷ 3 = 13 min (11.25 with the anomaly); 38 + 37 + 39 = 114, ÷ 3 = 38 °C; all four bounce readings give 47.5 cm. Ranges: 2.6 − 2.4 = 0.2 vs 2.9 − 2.0 = 0.9 s; 58 − 46 = 12 vs 53 − 52 = 1 cm; 21 − 20 = 1 vs 24 − 15 = 9. Definitions follow the ASE/Nuffield Language of Measurement (2010): precise = close together, accurate = close to the true value, repeatable, anomaly outside the expected spread; random error (reaction time) vs systematic error (unzeroed scale). Parameterised items keep the stated largest/smallest true at every corner (b ≥ 2, c ≥ 3).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: expecting identical repeat readings (Allen 2014; step 1 prediction, tag 'exact', m2), one reading being enough ('once', m6), averaging in the anomaly (step 3 prediction and the tray refusing it, 'all', m3 distractor 11.25), deleting the anomaly from the record ('erase', habit cards), trusting bigger numbers over closer readings ('spread', m4) and treating precise as accurate ('accprec', m5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagrepeat is built on the repeat-reading mechanism itself: a ramp and stopwatch that return slightly different times on each run, tappable four-reading tables with one anomaly, an Add up tray that accepts only the readings that fit and shows the running total and ÷ 3, side-by-side dot plots of two groups with the range revealed on a wrong choice, and a measuring-habits sort. It is unlike 'Measuring accurately' (682, reading scales, zeroing, eye level) and the gate measured under 30% shingle overlap with every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner first sees variation happen (2.4, 2.6, 2.5 s), then finds anomalies in three contexts, then has to leave the anomaly out to finish the mean (the tray rejects it with the reason), then judges reliability by range from dot plots, and finally applies the habits. Each done line confirms the rule just used; the means and ranges are computed on screen from the learner's own choices.

predictions.evidence: Two predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then disproves: 'Yes: same run, same time' (the next three timings differ), and 'Yes: use every reading' for 61 cm (the tray refuses it and shows the mean of 43 cm from the three that agree).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions with tagged wrong options and specific messages: 'exact' (variation is normal), 'once' (one reading cannot reveal a slip), 'all' (that mean includes the anomaly, divide the other three), 'erase' (never rub out a reading), 'spread' (look at range, not size), 'accprec' (close together is precise; an unzeroed scale shifts every reading) and 'big' (that reading sits with the others).

readability.evidence: Learner lesson for ages 9 to 11: kid text FK 3.7 against the 6.5 limit, adult text FK 7.5 against 9.5 (rewritten into shorter sentences after a first draft scored 10.5). Each technical word (anomaly, mean, range, precise, accurate) is defined in a kid paragraph with a worked number example before it is used in the lab.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no filler phrases; under 12% overlap with any lesson, including 682 'Measuring accurately' and 679 'Calculating the Mean'). Kid paragraphs cover variation, anomalies, the mean without the anomaly and range with precise vs accurate; adult paragraphs give curriculum wording, ASE definitions with random and systematic error, good practice for anomalies, and named mistakes with a lab summary.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 (light) and 360 x 640 Android (dark) screenshots of all six steps: the ramp, stopwatch and three run rows fit side by side; the four reading tiles fit one row at 26 px with their 'Reading n' labels (a font bleed that overlapped the labels on the first screenshot was fixed); the tray holds three cards; the two group panels show dot plots with 14 px values. Buttons under the canvas wrap without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: 'Time a run', one button per reading naming its value ('Reading 4, 61 cm, is the anomaly'), 'Add 42 cm' buttons that skip drag, Group A and Group B, and Good or Not good practice naming the card. note() updates the canvas aria-label and the polite live region after every action; the walk gate's axe run (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13, and tiles keep dark ink on light fills in both themes.
